material_systems.name: Penetrating Stain Recoat (Transparent / Semi-Transparent)

products.product_name: Exterior penetrating wood stain — transparent or semi-transparent
products.manufacturer_example: Cabot Australian Timber Oil / TWP 100 Series
products.notes: Penetrating oil or water-based stain. Must match existing stain chemistry (oil-over-oil, water-over-water when possible). Direct recoat over serviceable penetrating stain — no primer.

material_systems.notes: Single coat penetrating recoat. Penetrating stains erode rather than peel — recoat goes directly over existing stain after cleaning. No primer. Back-brushing MANDATORY when spray applied.

material_systems.name: Solid Body Stain Recoat

products.manufacturer_example: Benjamin Moore Arborcoat Solid / Sherwin-Williams SuperDeck Solid
products.notes: Film-forming solid stain. Must be compatible with existing solid stain. 100% acrylic for flexibility on fence.

material_systems.notes: Film-forming recoat. QT2=1 coat, QT3=2 coats. May require primer if bare wood is exposed (peeling condition). Tannin-blocking primer on cedar when bare.

material_systems.name: Exterior Latex Paint Recoat (LEAST RECOMMENDED)

products.product_name: Exterior 100% acrylic latex paint — high permeability
products.manufacturer_example: Benjamin Moore Regal Select Exterior / Sherwin-Williams Duration Exterior
products.notes: LEAST RECOMMENDED for wood fences. High permeability formulation critical to allow moisture vapor transmission. 100% acrylic for maximum flexibility.

material_systems.notes: LEAST RECOMMENDED. Paint recoat on fence carries moisture-driven peeling risk. Mandatory risk warning documentation. Primer required on all bare wood areas.

material_systems.name: Alkyd Stain-Blocking Primer (Cedar Bare Wood)

products.manufacturer_example: Zinsser Cover Stain / KILZ Original Exterior
products.notes: MANDATORY on cedar bare wood exposed under peeling coating. Prevents tannin bleed through film-forming topcoat.

material_systems.notes: Conditional — only when bare cedar is exposed (peeling condition) AND topcoat is film-forming (solid stain or paint). NOT used for penetrating stain recoats.

material_systems.name: Standard Exterior Acrylic Primer (PT Pine Bare Wood)

products.manufacturer_example: Benjamin Moore Fresh Start Exterior / Sherwin-Williams PrepRite ProBlock
products.notes: Standard exterior primer for bare PT pine. Used when peeling coating exposes bare wood and topcoat is paint.

material_systems.notes: Conditional — only when bare PT pine is exposed AND topcoat is paint. Solid stain on PT pine does not require primer (even over bare wood — stain penetrates). Cedar uses stain-blocking primer instead.

material_systems.name: Fence Cleaner / Stripper (Alkaline)

products.manufacturer_example: Cabot Problem-Solver Wood Stripper / TWP Gemini Wood Stripper
products.notes: Reused from NC spec. First step in chemical restoration. MUST be neutralized with brightener.

material_systems.notes: Reused from NC. Conditional on weathered condition with coating removal needed.

material_systems.name: Wood Brightener (Oxalic / Citric Acid)

products.manufacturer_example: Cabot Problem-Solver Wood Brightener / TWP Gemini Brightener
products.notes: Reused from NC spec. Second step in chemical restoration. Neutralizes stripper, restores wood tone.

material_systems.notes: Reused from NC. Paired with chemical stripper for weathered fence restoration.

coverage_profiles.notes: Penetrating stain on previously stained wood. Existing stain reduces absorption vs bare wood — slightly higher coverage than NC first coat.
Solid stain recoat. Existing coating reduces absorption.
Paint recoat over existing paint. Film-to-film coverage.
Stain-blocking primer on bare cedar. Spot or full application.
Standard primer on bare PT pine.
Chemical stripper coverage. Heavy application required for weathered wood.

consumables.name: 4" stain brush
consumables.notes: Stain/paint brush for fence. Higher yield than trim brush — larger surface area per stroke.

consumables.name: Airless spray tip 517 (stain)
consumables.notes: Standard stain spray tip. Wider fan pattern for fence panels.

consumables.name: Airless spray tip 515 (paint)
consumables.notes: Paint spray tip — slightly narrower than stain tip.

consumables.name: 4" back-brush for spray staining
consumables.notes: Back-brush used immediately after spray pass. MANDATORY for penetrating stains.

consumables.name: 80-grit sandpaper sheet
consumables.notes: Heavy sanding for peeling/failing paint removal and feather-edging.

consumables.name: 100-grit sandpaper sheet
consumables.notes: General sanding for scuff/adhesion prep on sound coatings.

consumables.name: 5" paint scraper
consumables.notes: Paint/stain scraper for peeling coating removal.

consumables.name: Wire brush (hand)
consumables.notes: Wire brush for removing loose coating and weathered fibers.

consumables.name: Plastic sheeting 10x25 ft
consumables.notes: Ground protection along fence base. Both sides.

consumables.name: Canvas drop cloth 4x15 ft
consumables.notes: Heavy-duty protection for hardscape areas along fence.

consumables.name: 2" blue painters tape
consumables.notes: Masking at fence-to-house junction and gate hardware.

consumables.name: 12" masking paper
consumables.notes: Masking paper for siding protection at fence tie.

consumables.name: Pin-type moisture meter (rental/shared)
consumables.notes: Moisture content testing. Reusable tool. One per project.
